observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: A painterly weeping willow on transparent alpha. It has a thick, twisted, multi-forked trunk in purple-black bark with moss patches, splitting into several leaning limbs. Long blue-green strands of narrow leaves hang in separate curtains from three or four crown lobes. The canopy is open and irregular, not a dome: wide gaps show the trunk and limbs from the base up to the crown. Most strands stop between one half and three quarters of the way down; only a few at the outer edges reach near the bottom. The root flare sits at the bottom centre with a faint mossy scatter and no ground disc. The tree fills almost the whole canvas and is roughly as wide as it is tall.

Max zoom (cropped): the hanging strands and the gnarled root flare stay crisp, with fine leaf detail and no visible upscaling. Normal play at 32 px/cell: the tree spans about 9–10 cells and stands several times the human's height, reading clearly as a weeping tree with a dark trunk and teal curtains. The open canopy and visible trunk are obvious at this zoom too.
